chapter: Chicago in the 1920s: Bix, Armstrong, Morton
title: Seeing Jelly Roll Morton at the Elite No. 2 as a child
summary: Howard's aunt sang at the Elite No. 2 at 35th and State, where as a boy in short pants he saw Morton playing piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: When did you first see General Morton? Hmm? When did you first see General Morton?

I got news for you. My aunt was working at the Eli Number Two, Johnny Rose up on the stand. I'm up there with short pants. See they let me play in there because my aunt was working there. What was Eli Number Two? 35th and State. Was it a club? Yeah, a night spot. A night spot. He mentions it in that record, you know? I know. I don't know. He got it a little mixed up, though. I don't think he ever worked at 31st Street. That's the original Eli. I see. But he worked at 35th Street. And I'm sitting up there in short pants. He's the one who wrote the journal, old boy. Oh yeah. Is that where he wrote it?
Yes, at the Eli Number Two. Were you working there with him? Yeah. Was it his band? No. Whose band was it? Olive.

Olive. You would have asked that, wait a minute. Harry Mattsengill was a trombone player. I don't know whether it was his band or the, see they had funny combinations and they had trombone and a four piece combination. Yes. Gordon was playing piano in this band? Uh-huh. Maybe my aunt could help me out because she was working the courses to do this. There ain't no way to help them out. She was singing there, huh? Yeah. Singing and dancing there. Singing and dancing there. Florence Mills was too. Oh yeah? Yes, wait a minute. Florence Mills, Cora Green, and my aunt. There were three women singing there. Oh yeah? And they had a firm name of Crump. Oh yeah.
Jesse Crump? No. Oh no, not him. What kind of a guy was you little at that time? Full of notoriety. Full of notoriety.

Good guy, but it was full of notoriety. Uh-huh. Oh yeah. Why? I guess because he could be, I thought. No particular reason. Was he popular at the time? Well, at least I can remember them. They liked his work very well. They did? Oh heck yes. Not another piano player was playing like he was playing. He was style, you know. Yeah? Oh yeah. He played that.
